questions.prompt: You set `max_tokens: 5` and the reply ends with `finish_reason: "length"`. What does that tell you?
options: The model finished its answer in exactly 5 tokens
The reply was cut off by the 5-token limit and is probably incomplete
The model wants your program to run a function
The request was rejected for being too long
questions.explanation: `length` means a token limit stopped the reply. With a limit of 5 the text ends wherever the fifth token fell, not where the model meant to stop.

questions.prompt: Your program only reads `message.content` and ignores `finish_reason`. What can go wrong?
options: Nothing, because a cut-off reply is always empty
The provider charges for the unread field
A truncated reply looks like a complete one, so the program may act on half an answer
The model repeats its reply in the next request
questions.explanation: A cut-off reply is ordinary-looking text. Only the stop reason says it was truncated, so ignoring it means treating half a list or half a block of code as finished.

questions.prompt: A reply arrives with a `finish_reason` value your code does not recognise. What is the safe thing to do?
options: Treat it as a failure rather than a finished answer
Treat it as `stop` and show the text
Send the same request again forever until it says `stop`
Delete the reply from the history and continue
questions.explanation: Only `stop` means the model finished by itself. An unknown reason gives no such promise, so handling it as a failure avoids acting on a reply that may be incomplete.
